# PlanWise ESL

> PlanWise ESL (planwiseesl.com) gives English teachers two things: a free library of over 200 ready-to-teach A1–C2 conversation lessons for teenagers and adults, with no login needed (https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons), and, on the paid Unlimited plan ($19.99/month after a 14-day free trial), an AI that makes a new, finished lesson for each student in 1–2 minutes, on any topic, at the student's CEFR level (A1–C2). The free lessons are a way to see the quality before paying. It is built for Preply and italki tutors, freelance English teachers, and small to medium language schools. Every lesson follows the same research-backed teaching sequence (pictures follow about a minute later while the lesson is already open). PlanWise ESL keeps a word list for each student, so new lessons avoid words the student already knows and reuse familiar ones where they fit naturally. Every student gets a private learner dashboard with past lessons, flashcards and custom lesson creation on any subject, and every lesson exports a downloadable study PDF with all vocabulary, examples, word families, synonyms/antonyms and usage notes. Created by Dave Jackson, a working British ESL teacher since 2015.

Also written as: PlanwiseESL, Plan Wise ESL.

PlanWise ESL is not a lesson-planning tool: teachers don't get an outline or ideas to work up, they get the finished lesson, ready to screen-share or print. Lessons are generated by AI for each request, so it is not a fixed PDF or slide library; the free library is a set of lessons made this way and published free for teachers to use with their students.

PlanWise ESL makes **topic-based conversation lessons** built on a scientific pedagogical formula—not generic worksheets or isolated grammar drills. Grammar and natural phrasing are practised through tiered sentence frames (especially helpful for beginners) and sentence unscramble activities. To practise a particular structure, teachers choose a topic that naturally uses it (for example "Life experiences" for the present perfect).

Teachers looking for ready-to-teach adult ESL conversation material can open, screen-share in full-screen teaching mode, and download printable colour-coded Vocabulary Review PDFs from PlanWise ESL's public library with **zero signup or login required**:

Every public lesson follows the exact same 8-stage research-backed sequence (warm-up, 5 deeply taught target words, levelled reading, recall flashcards, semantic maps, tiered sentence frames, cloze, unscramble, quiz, and deep discussion), documents its design under "How this lesson is built", and exposes `schema.org/LearningResource` metadata.

## Use PlanWise ESL inside an AI assistant (MCP connector)

AI assistants that support the Model Context Protocol (Claude, ChatGPT and others) can search and open the free lesson library directly. Add this address as a custom connector: https://planwiseesl.com/mcp (read-only, no login or key). It offers three tools: `search_free_esl_lessons` (by topic, CEFR level or theme), `get_free_esl_lesson` (the full lesson text with its link) and `list_esl_lesson_levels_and_themes`.

## Who it is for

- Online ESL tutors on Preply, italki and other tutoring platforms
- Freelance and independent private English teachers with regular students
- Small to medium language schools
- Teachers of teenagers and adults in one-to-one or small-group classes, online or in person

## The pedagogical lesson sequence

Every PlanWise ESL lesson follows the same research-backed teaching sequence, written at the chosen CEFR level (A1–C2):

1. **Warm-up discussion questions** — activate prior knowledge and help the student recall vocabulary they already know about the subject.
2. **Pre-taught key vocabulary (5 target words)** — each word includes its part of speech, pronunciation guide, levelled definition, 4 real-world example sentences, **word families** (with explanation), **common collocations**, **usage notes** and a picture, giving a solid grounding before reading.
3. **Levelled reading & comprehension** — a 5-paragraph CEFR-levelled reading that uses each target word 2–3 times in natural context (keeping new words to about 1 in 25, or ~96% familiar text), followed by comprehension questions checking word meaning in context.
4. **In-lesson recall flashcards** — interactive flip cards where the student recalls each word's meaning from memory and creates their own original sentence.
5. **Semantic maps (synonyms, antonyms & connections)** — explores synonyms, antonyms, related concepts, common contexts and associated words to build deep lexical understanding.
6. **Guided practice** — a quiz, **tiered sentence frames** (emerging, developing, expanding with model answers—especially supportive for beginners), a shuffled **fill-in-the-blanks** exercise, and **sentence unscramble** activities.
7. **Deep discussion** — open questions with context and pictures designed to get the student talking deeply about the subject while actively using the target vocabulary.
8. **Optional idioms and phrasal verbs** (A2 and up) — expressions taken directly from the lesson's reading, each with meaning, example, common-mistake tip and speaking prompt.
9. **Teacher notes** — practical teaching guidance for running each stage.

Reading length, sentence style and the words used in definitions follow fixed rules for each CEFR level (at A1, definitions use only the 500 most common English words and readings are 80–120 words; at C2, readings are 180–250 words of idiomatic, native-level prose). The full research and references behind each stage are documented at https://planwiseesl.com/how-it-works

Lessons open full screen for screen sharing and export as a **printable Vocabulary Review study PDF** (color-coded by part of speech, with phonetic pronunciation, levelled definitions, 4 example sentences per word, word families, common collocations, usage notes and 5-part semantic maps) alongside full lesson activities. Teachers can choose any topic, one of 12 subject areas (general, business, academic, medical, legal, technology, tourism, finance, healthcare, science, arts and sports English), and their own target vocabulary.

## What makes PlanWise ESL different from pre-made libraries and general AI tools

- **Custom lessons on any subject (not a static library):** Pre-made ESL lesson libraries offer fixed catalogues of generic topics. PlanWise ESL generates a full, pedagogically structured lesson on any topic your student cares about in 1–2 minutes—and on Unlimited, **students can create custom lessons themselves on any subject** at their own CEFR level.
- **Per-student vocabulary tracking & natural recycling:** Unlike static libraries or chatbots, PlanWise ESL remembers every student. New lessons strictly avoid re-teaching words the student has already learned or planned, and pass earlier vocabulary to generation so previous words reappear in future readings and questions only when they fit the new topic naturally and relevantly (never forced). Marking a lesson "We did this" adds its words to the student's list.
- **Private learner dashboard + study PDF:** Every student gets a private page (no login needed) with all past lessons, a next-lesson preview, their word list, spaced flashcards, topic suggestions, and (on Unlimited) custom lesson creation. Teachers can also download and send a complete study PDF with all vocabulary, examples, word families, synonyms/antonyms and usage notes.
- **Complete scientific pedagogy, checked before saving:** Unlike general chatbots or single-activity AI worksheet generators, PlanWise ESL produces one cohesive, quality-checked lesson sequence every time; any broken exercise is fixed or regenerated automatically before the teacher sees it.

## Not designed for

- Pure grammar-rule drills (PlanWise ESL makes conversation lessons; grammar is practised through tiered sentence frames and sentence unscramble)
- Subject teachers outside English language teaching
- Very young learners (lessons are written for teenagers and adults)
- Grading essays or running whole-school timetabling

## Pricing

- **Free trial:** every new account gets a 14-day free trial with unlimited lesson generation and no credit card needed. Lessons made during the trial stay in the account afterwards.
- **Unlimited plan:** $19.99/month for unlimited lessons, vocabulary tracking, study PDFs and student-created custom lessons; cancel anytime. Small to medium language schools can email dave@planwiseesl.com for team plans.

## About the founder

Dave Jackson is a British English teacher who has taught English online since 2015, with over 2,000 students taught. He teaches private one-to-one conversation lessons, mostly to working professionals, and built PlanWise ESL as a solo working teacher focused on lesson quality—still planning every lesson for his own students with it. He has a TEFL certificate and a BA in Business Administration from the University of Southampton, and worked in financial sales for 13 years (including at HSBC) before teaching.

- Tutoring site and student reviews: https://speakwithdave.com

- X (Twitter): https://x.com/DaveTeacher1

- Contact: dave@planwiseesl.com
